title: Structural Organisation in Animals
tagline: Animal tissues — epithelial, connective, muscular and nervous — and a brief account of frog systems with diagrams.

sourceNote.boardprep: Original study material written by BoardPrep for the CISCE ISC Class XI Biology syllabus (official-verified baseline, examination year 2027). Syllabus unit and chapter title were taken from the official-verified ISC Biology registry entry; no board examination paper was consulted, so every question is original practice and not a previous year question.

overview.intro: Animals are built from cells, but most of their functions depend on tissues, which are groups of similar cells working together. This chapter begins with the four main types of animal tissue: epithelial, connective, muscular and nervous. We then look at how tissues are organised into organs and organ systems. As a familiar example, a brief account of frog systems is included, with the structures shown clearly in diagrams, because the syllabus asks for that kind of organised description.

facts.label: Syllabus unit
facts.value: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants

facts.label: Core ideas
facts.value: Epithelial, connective, muscular and nervous tissues; organs and organ systems; brief frog systems with diagrams

learningOutcomes: Define animal tissue and distinguish tissue from organ.
Describe the four main tissue types and their functions.
Give examples of each tissue type.
Explain how tissues form organs and organ systems.
Give a brief account of frog systems with labelled diagrams.

blocks.text: Epithelial tissue covers body surfaces and lines cavities and tubes. Its cells are closely packed and often rest on a basement membrane. Depending on its arrangement and shape, epithelial tissue may protect, absorb, secrete or filter. Skin, the lining of the gut and the lining of blood vessels are all examples of epithelial tissue in different forms.

items: Epithelial tissue covers surfaces and lines cavities.
It may protect, absorb, secrete or filter.

items.text: The inner lining of the small intestine is epithelial tissue specialised for absorption, while the outer layer of skin is epithelial tissue specialised for protection.
items.note: The same basic tissue type can be adapted for very different jobs.

blocks.text: Connective tissue links and supports other tissues and organs. Its cells are usually spaced apart by an intercellular matrix, which may be fluid or solid. Blood, bone, cartilage and adipose tissue are all connective tissues, but they look very different because their matrix varies. The main function is support, protection, connection or transport, depending on the type.

items: The matrix may be fluid or solid.
Examples include blood, bone, cartilage and fat tissue.

items.text: Bone is a connective tissue with a hard matrix, giving strength and support. Blood is a connective tissue with a fluid matrix, suited to transport.
items.note: The diversity of connective tissue is one reason it is easy to confuse different kinds if you only remember the name.

blocks.text: Muscular tissue is specialised for contraction and movement. There are different kinds of muscle tissue, including those responsible for voluntary movement and those found in internal organs. Nervous tissue is specialised for receiving stimuli and transmitting electrical signals. Together, muscle and nervous tissue allow the body to move, coordinate and respond to the environment.

items: Muscular tissue contracts to produce movement.
Different muscle types have different roles.

items.text: Skeletal muscle moves bones, while nervous tissue carries signals from the brain and spinal cord to muscles and sense organs.
items.note: Movement is often the result of several tissue types working together, not muscle alone.

blocks.text: The frog is used as a familiar example of a vertebrate body plan. Its major systems include the digestive, circulatory, respiratory, excretory, nervous and reproductive systems. Each system has organs with related functions, and each is made up of several tissue types. A brief account of these systems should be supported by labelled diagrams, because structure and function are best understood together.

items: The frog has digestive, circulatory, respiratory, excretory, nervous and reproductive systems.
Each system has organs with specific functions.
Organs are made of multiple tissues.
Diagrams help show structure and relationship.

items.text: The heart is an organ of the circulatory system, made largely of muscular tissue for pumping, with other tissues for support and control.
items.note: The heart illustrates how an organ combines tissues for a single overall function.

keyPoints: A tissue is a group of similar cells performing a function.
The four main animal tissues are epithelial, connective, muscular and nervous.
Epithelial tissue covers surfaces and lines cavities.
Connective tissue supports and connects, with a varied matrix.
Muscular tissue contracts; nervous tissue transmits signals.
Organs contain several tissues working together.
Frog systems should be studied briefly with diagrams.
examFocus: When asked for tissues, give the function as well as the name; a tissue without its function is usually an incomplete answer.
Do not confuse an organ with a tissue; a heart is an organ, not a tissue.

vocabulary.meaning: A group of similar cells together with associated intercellular material, performing a specific function.
Tissue that covers surfaces and lines cavities.
Tissue that supports, connects or transports, usually with a prominent matrix.
Tissue specialised for contraction and movement.
Tissue specialised for receiving and transmitting signals.
A structure made of several tissues working together for a function.

questions.prompt: Which tissue type is mainly responsible for movement by contraction?
questions.explanation: Muscular tissue contracts to produce movement.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing nervous tissue, which transmits signals, not directly producing contraction.

questions.explanation: Blood is a connective tissue with a fluid matrix.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing epithelial tissue because blood lines vessels.

questions.prompt: Distinguish epithelial tissue from connective tissue.
questions.answer: Epithelial tissue has closely packed cells and covers surfaces or lines cavities. Connective tissue has cells separated by a matrix and supports, connects or transports.
questions.explanation: The main differences are cell packing and matrix.
questions.commonMistake: Only naming them without saying what makes them different.

questions.prompt: Why is a heart considered an organ rather than a tissue?
questions.answer: Because it is made of several tissue types, such as muscular tissue and others, working together for a single function.
questions.explanation: An organ contains multiple tissues, not just one.
questions.commonMistake: Saying it is an organ only because it is bigger, without mentioning tissues.

questions.prompt: Describe the functions of the four main animal tissues and give one example of each.
questions.answer: Epithelial tissue covers and lines surfaces and may protect, absorb or secrete, for example skin or intestinal lining. Connective tissue supports and connects, for example bone or blood. Muscular tissue contracts for movement, for example skeletal muscle. Nervous tissue transmits signals, for example brain tissue.
questions.explanation: A good answer links each tissue type to its function and an example.
questions.commonMistake: Giving only examples without the functions, or mixing up the tissue types.
